h: The Journeys Teach Active Holiness and the Healing of Shabbos

p: אֵלֶּה מַסְעֵי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר לג, א)
"These are the journeys of the Children of Israel," etc. (Bamidbar 33:1).
a matter whose secret has not been revealed to us;
not as Rabbi Avraham ibn Ezra said,
who said that it is joined to 'for their journeys,'
for the Torah has already informed us of that:
'By the word of Hashem they would encamp
וְעַל פִּי ה׳ יִסָּעוּ (בְּמִדְבַּר ט, כ)
and by the word of Hashem they would journey' (Bamidbar 9:20)";
In truth, this is explained in the Midrash
(רַבָּה וְתַנְחוּמָא; בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה כג, ג; תַּנְחוּמָא מַסְעֵי ג)
(Rabbah and Tanchuma; Bamidbar Rabbah 23:3, Tanchuma Masei 3)
which says: "A parable of a king
he took him to another place to heal him.
כָּךְ אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
So HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him:
This is what is said: "And Moshe wrote," etc.,
in accordance with the words of the Ramban, of blessed memory,
and not like the Ibn Ezra,
who wrote that it is joined to "for their journeys,"
from which it would appear that the writing of the journeys
was not a command of Hashem,
but rather Moshe wrote it on his own.
And the reason is found in the Midrash:
It is found (Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Parshas Beshalach, Beshalach 1):
"If I lead them by the straight road,
at once each man will take hold
and they will eat the manna
and drink the water of the well,
and the Torah will settle into their bodies."
שֶׁהֲרֵי בַּתּוֹרָה מְפוֹרָשׁ הַטַּעַם (שְׁמוֹת יג, יז)
for the reason is stated explicitly in the Torah (Shemos 13:17):
so how does the Midrash give a different reason?
But in truth it is all one:
for after they had left Egypt
and because of this there was fear
the people would reconsider and return to Egypt.
This is what it says in the parable,
and he took him to another place to heal him;
that is, He led them into the wilderness
so that they would eat manna
and drink the water of the well,
and the Torah would settle into their bodies.
This is the matter of the journeys and the encampments:
for there to be an encampment afterward.
there would have been, immediately after the first journey,
like that of the future, in the World to Come.
"And the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem journeyed before them
to seek out a resting place for them";
for they were fit to merit,
to be refined in all three holinesses of the Avos,
and to be saved from the three kelipos opposite them,
which are the roots of all the kelipos;
and that afterward there would be the rest
But it is as with Shabbos:
through the keeping of one Shabbos
as it should be, they are immediately redeemed
(as they said in the Yerushalmi, first perek of Taanis,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח, ב)
and nevertheless it says in the Gemara (Shabbos 118b):
as they should be, they would immediately be redeemed."
And we said that it is all one:
of the first Shabbos as it should be,
into the weekdays that follow it,
Now the world is judged according to its majority,
and when the majority of Yisrael
keep two Shabbosos as they should be,
that there should not be a number of individual souls
who keep Shabbos as it should be;
so why were they not redeemed
and from the Angel of Death,
But in truth, the intent of
"one who keeps Shabbos as it should be"
is not that it suffices for him to guard
merely by sitting and not acting
Rather, the meaning of "as it should be"
is that one must bring holiness
"And the Children of Israel shall keep the Shabbos"
that it become the upper Shabbos.
And this is a Shabbos kept as it should be,
through which one is immediately redeemed entirely.

p: there had to be a preparation for the encampment,
not only by sitting and not acting,
by emptying the evil out of the fool's heart;
אַךְ צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב
This is what the parable says:
in which there was a deficiency
in attaining the perfection of the encampment
that it be as in the future,
that is, although there was "turn from evil,"
This is why it says "we slept,"
along the lines of what they said:
"One who sits idle is like one who sleeps."
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּכוֹרוֹת ה, ב)
along the lines of what they said (Bechoros 5b):
That they slackened themselves from the words of Torah."
This is what it says, "here we were chilled":
for this is the kelipah of Amalek,
"who happened upon you on the way"
for he casts coldness and sadness
even though they were "turn from evil."
than the deficiency of "here we slept";
שֶׁזֶּהוּ רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק (בְּמִדְבַּר כד, כ)
for this is "Amalek, the first of nations" (Bamidbar 24:20)
which comes from the Serpent and the yetzer hara;
לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י)
"'That it may not grieve me' (Divrei HaYamim I 4:10):
that the yetzer hara not overpower me
so that I cease from learning."
And it says, "Here your head ached,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת יא, א)
along the lines of what they said (Shabbos 11a):
but not an ache of the head";
"an ache is merely a passing discomfort,
that it was an ache of the head.
This is why it says, "your head ached."
נִכְלַל הַמֶּלֶךְ גַּם כֵּן עִם בְּנוֹ
the king includes himself together with his son;
which is not so with the third deficiency,
which he said in the second person, to the son alone.
"And Hashem awoke as one who sleeps."
for the encampment to be as it should be
עַל יְדֵי וַעֲשֵׂה טוֹב גַּם כֵּן
עַל יְדֵי זֶה גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
because of this Hashem Yisbarach too,
as it were, was like one asleep,
and did not help with heavenly assistance
And so with "here we were chilled":
as it were, Hashem Yisbarach too
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שְׁמוֹת יז, יא)
along the lines of what is said (Shemos 17:11):
"And it was, when Moshe raised his hand,
to their Father in Heaven," etc.
instilled in the heart of Yisrael
But without an arousal from below,
there was no arousal from above.
This is not so with the third deficiency,
which was a deficiency in deed,
even though it was only for the moment,
Hashem Yisbarach did not include Himself with them,
they only open the way for him;
one who comes to purify himself, they assist him."
And it lists all the names of the journeys,
and whoever has a heart to understand
that they did not merit the true encampment
And the name of the encampment proves this:
and sometimes it was an ache of the head
that it is not enough to keep the day of Shabbos,
which is a day of rest,
rather, there must also be "do good,"
and it is expounded (in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48):
"Fortunate is he who makes for them a dwelling
in the two chambers of the heart,
and the yetzer hara is cleared out from there";
and that is the rest as in the future.
And it is written, "And Moshe wrote
אֶת מוֹצָאֵיהֶם לְמַסְעֵיהֶם עַל פִּי ה׳
their goings forth for their journeys by the word of Hashem";
that is, since he was commanded
and this was written by the word of Hashem.
before which there was no encampment,
only the first journey out of Egypt
this Moshe Rabbeinu was not commanded
for the first journey, from Ra'amses,
was the preparation for the first encampment.
"And these are their journeys by their goings forth:
And they journeyed from Ra'amses," etc. (Bamidbar 33:2–3).
לֹא כְּתִיב כָּאן עַל פִּי ה׳
"by the word of Hashem" is not written here,
for this refers to the first journey,
וְזֶה לֹא נִכְתַּב עַל פִּי ה׳
and that was not written by the word of Hashem.
This is why the change came
in the wording of the pasuk:
that at first it is written
and "by the word of Hashem" is not written.
